name: entity_tokens_in_text
rationale: Gold entities are exact token spans of the text, and the label compares lower-cased values, so every correct string matches a contiguous run of lower-cased tokens. This catches invented, paraphrased or partially fabricated strings.

name: entity_has_letter
rationale: CoNLL entities always contain at least one letter. This catches outputs that extract numbers, scores or dates such as "1", "0-0" or "1996-08-26".

name: no_empty_string_entity
rationale: Gold lists never contain empty strings, because the lists are compared after stripping and no gold entity is blank. This catches outputs containing "" or whitespace-only entries.

name: multiplicity_not_exceeding_text
rationale: Each gold entity corresponds to a distinct mention, so a string cannot be listed more often than it occurs as a token span in the text. This catches outputs that repeat an entity spuriously.

name: no_boundary_punctuation
rationale: Gold spans never begin or end with a pure punctuation token such as a comma, parenthesis or quote. This catches sloppy spans like "Hungary (" or ", Reuters".

name: no_possessive_end
rationale: CoNLL gold excludes the possessive "'s" token from entities. This catches spans like "Malawi 's".

name: no_leading_lowercase_determiner
rationale: A span that begins with a lower-case "the", "a" or "an" in every occurrence in the text is never a gold entity. This catches spans like "the Dodgers".

name: no_pronoun_entity
rationale: Pronouns are never named entities. This catches outputs that extract "he", "they" or similar words.

name: no_weekday_entity
rationale: CoNLL does not tag days of the week. This catches outputs that list "Monday" or "Thursday" as entities.

name: no_reporting_verb_inside
rationale: Gold entity spans do not contain lower-case reporting verbs or copulas. This catches over-long spans like "Shehu told Reuters".

name: no_lowercase_title_start
rationale: CoNLL gold excludes lower-case titles and descriptors such as "president" or "former". This catches spans like "former president" or "minister X".

name: entity_not_too_long
rationale: No CoNLL entity spans more than 12 tokens. This catches outputs that dump whole clauses or sentences into a field.

name: total_entities_bounded_by_tokens
rationale: Gold entities are non-overlapping token spans, so there can be no more of them than there are tokens in the text. This catches hallucinated padding.

name: no_all_stopword_entity
rationale: An entity made up entirely of lower-case function words, such as "of the", is never a gold entity. This catches junk extractions.

name: no_entity_with_dollar
rationale: Money amounts are not entities in CoNLL. This catches outputs that extract spans containing a "$" token.

name: no_full_sentence_entity
rationale: A whole sentence of six or more tokens is never a single entity. This catches outputs that copy the entire text into a field.

name: no_lowercase_common_noun_else
rationale: Only a few well-known lower-case common nouns are covered here, and a span whose every occurrence in the text is one of these lower-case words is never gold. This catches extractions like "war", "meeting" or "record" in the else field.

name: no_month_alone_lowercase_context
rationale: CoNLL does not tag month names. A bare month is rejected only when every occurrence in the text is directly followed by a number, i.e. it is clearly a date. This catches outputs that extract "January" from "January 1".

name: no_trailing_lowercase_common_word
rationale: A span that ends with a lower-case token like "refugees", "embassy" or "boost" in every occurrence in the text is an over-extension of the real entity. This catches spans like "Albanian refugees" and "Greek embassy".

name: no_pure_lowercase_hyphen_phrase
rationale: Multi-token spans whose tokens are all lower-case in the text and all contain no digits are not CoNLL entities. To stay safe against the known "interior ministry" gold, spans containing "ministry" are exempted. This catches extractions like "alien-led profit boost" and "wild card".
